correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and the Kirchhoff-index normalization are stated. Strict convexity of trace-inverse over a connected edge-weight simplex proves global uniqueness. Graph automorphisms force three edge classes; the two invariant page-difference spaces and two quotient blocks give an exact rational spectral identity. A strict negative feasible derivative excludes zero middle-edge weights, leaving one optional bridge. The reduced no-bridge problem has a unique positive stationary ratio and a KKT derivative with sign g_m(r_m)(d-d_m*). This proves the exact support threshold, including equality. The leading polynomial and its simple positive root establish the 1/m asymptotic. A self-contained standard-library exact rational verifier passed 124 checks; finite checks do not substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The object is an intrinsically motivated set of parallel three-edge routes with a purchasable shortcut. The claimed support boundary decides whether an entire edge class should be funded, remains exact for arbitrarily many pages and arbitrary budgets, and supplies a new 1/m network-size asymptotic. The classification also proves that every middle edge remains essential in the optimized design; it is a structural result, not an arbitrary small-graph computation.
